summary.intent: Get an ADR written and opened as a PR that records a decision for the resolver to own name scoping, delegating the drafting to a subagent and then verifying and reporting on the result.
summary.outcome: PR #374 (docs/adr-scoping-one-owner) is open as a draft adding ADR 0025 'The resolver owns scoping' plus an index line; the commit shows a good signature, but CI had only just started and the PR is not yet ready to merge.

repo: ADRs live in docs/adr/ with an index line in docs/adr/README.md; formatting is checked with oxfmt and spelling with typos.
Lint and doc checks are run via `just lint` and `just doc-check`; `just lint` calls `pnpm exec`, which needs network access to install deps.
The doc build uses `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi`.
Cache invalidation is controlled by `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`; adding scope identity to collected declarations needs a bump.
Resolver branches are expected to be measured on Chakra plus dependencies for peak memory and time.
docs/edge-cases.md describes the behavior where local aliases and enums replace module-level ones of the same name.

code.finding: `TypeScope` binds type parameters only, and its doc comment says declarations sit at module level. There is no declaration scoping to extend yet, so the ADR says 'TypeScope or a sibling type'.
`ImportRef` lives here, not in extractor/import_map.rs. Only this file's tests read `is_type_only`; the resolver reads it nowhere.
`promote_reexported_imports` is the only non-test reader of `ImportBinding.is_type_only`, so type-only status is currently decided by the extractor's re-export promotion.

`local_depth` is read only by `visit_ts_interface_declaration`. The alias and enum collectors insert under `scoped_key` unconditionally, so a local alias or enum replaces a module-level one of the same name.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output without user authority; the assistant read the ADR and checked the commit signature itself rather than trusting the report.
Read CI results by job name (the Lint job) rather than assuming a docs-only change is covered by the worker's partial local checks.
Start dependent follow-up work only after the ADR merges; the user's acceptance of the ADR is the decision gate.

friction: The subagent sandbox blocked network access, so the worktree could not install deps and `just lint` failed at `pnpm exec`.
The subagent had to borrow the main checkout's node_modules/.bin/oxfmt to run the formatter.
zsh `PIPESTATUS` was empty, so the exit code of `cargo doc` could not be read directly.
The subagent did not confirm commit signature status or run a clean-room worktree check; the assistant verified the signature separately.
The ADR's Context cites no review-finding numbers because none could be shown.
open_items: Wait for PR #374 CI to finish and read the Lint job by name before it is considered mergeable.
User needs to accept the ADR (merge) as the decision.
Follow-up branch 1: add scope identity to collected declarations with no reader yet, bumping CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION; to be started only after merge.
Follow-up branch 2: resolve interfaces by scope and drop `local_depth` and `module_interfaces`.
Follow-up branch 3: give a `switch` case its own scope.
Follow-up branch 4: do the same for aliases and enums, then classes.
Follow-up branch 5: read `ImportRef.is_type_only` in the resolver, or remove the field.
Two other workers (defaults contract and `InvalidJson`) are still running and need reports.
